title: GLOBAL SPEC — ANALYTICAL ARCHETYPE (SAP Analytical List Page)
purpose:
THE MIDDLE THING, AND THE ONE MOST PRODUCTS MISS. SAP: the ALP "offers a unique way to analyse data step by step from different perspectives, to investigate a ROOT CAUSE through drilldown, AND TO ACT ON TRANSACTIONAL CONTENT. All this can be done seamlessly WITHIN ONE PAGE."
DASHBOARD tells you something is wrong. ANALYTICAL tells you WHY and lets you FIX IT WITHOUT LEAVING. REPORT proves it to someone else.
*** THIS IS WHERE A DASHBOARD CLICK LANDS. Without it every KPI either dead-ends or dumps the user into a raw table with no context — which is what PROJEXA does today. ***
SAP's stated benefit, worth repeating to Sumeet: users get "fully transparent business object data AND direct access to business actions... without having to switch between systems", and "visualisation enables them to identify spikes, deviations and abnormalities quickly, and to TAKE APPROPRIATE ACTION RIGHT AWAY."
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Breadcrumb "Analysis · Cost variance · Villa 21". Almost always arrived at BY CLICKING A DASHBOARD KPI OR CHART SEGMENT, with filters pre-applied and visibly stated.
document_level: ORG + HEADER + ITEM. Drills to a single ITEM.
input_values:
THREE-AREA STRUCTURE (SAP ALP, adopted as-is):
 1. PAGE TITLE — up to THREE global KPI tags, no more (SAP's own limit, and a good one). Clicking a tag opens its KPI card with a chart.
 2. PAGE HEADER — filter area with TWO MODES THE USER TOGGLES:
    NORMAL FILTER BAR: standard controls per M30 cardinality.
    *** VISUAL FILTERS: each filter is ITSELF A SMALL INTERACTIVE CHART. The user filters BY CLICKING A BAR rather than reading a dropdown. For a site engineer this is the biggest comprehension win available — he sees the distribution AND filters in one act. ***
 3. PAGE CONTENT — three toggleable views: HYBRID (chart + table), CHART ONLY, TABLE ONLY. All three always available; default HYBRID.
Selection in the chart filters the table and vice versa. That interplay is the point.
displays:
HYBRID VIEW, chart above / table below:
 CHART: sorted horizontal bar by default (comparison is the usual question), switchable to line for time. Clicking a bar SLICES the table beneath.
 TABLE: the transactional rows in full detail, same importance-ranked columns as a LIST.
 VARIANT MANAGEMENT (SAP): the user SAVES A VIEW — filter mode, filter values, view switch state, chart measures and dimensions, sort, drill state. Personal or public, optionally the new default.
 *** THIS IS v5 D-5/D-7 IN PRACTICE: a saved view is DATA, personal by default, promoted to public only by Rajat. L2 may PROPOSE a view; it never publishes one. ***
 DRILL STATE VISIBLE AS A BREADCRUMB OF SLICES: "All > Category: Joinery > Trade: Carpentry", each independently removable. A user who cannot see how they reached a number does not trust it.
actions:
*** ACT IN PLACE — THIS IS WHAT MAKES IT ANALYTICAL RATHER THAN A CHART. Table rows carry the SAME actions as their LIST screen. Found the over-budget line? Record progress, open the BOQ line, raise a variation — from this row, without navigating away. ***
 EVERY ROW LINKS to its OBJECT screen. Every chart segment drills. Every KPI tag opens its card.
 CROSS-NAVIGATION: an action may hand off to another function_id with parameters bound (SAP semantic-object navigation) — from an over-budget line straight into "New variation" pre-filled with that line.
 HEADER: Filter | Export | + New. Export = the CURRENT SLICE as XLSX with the drill breadcrumb printed in it.
 SAVE VIEW | RESET VIEW alongside.
next_step: Row click -> OBJECT. Row action -> that function's FORM, pre-filled. Chart click -> deeper slice, same page, new URL. KPI tag -> KPI card. Save view -> stays, confirms.
cognitive_load:
THE USER NEVER LOSES THE THREAD: the drill breadcrumb shows every slice, each removable independently. BACK REMOVES ONE SLICE, NOT ALL OF THEM.
VISUAL FILTERS REMOVE A WHOLE READING STEP — the distribution and the control are the same object.
Chart and table always show THE SAME DATA. If they can disagree, the screen is broken.
THREE KPI TAGS MAXIMUM. More would make this a dashboard, and a dashboard-that-drills is neither thing done well.
Default HYBRID because most users need the shape AND the rows; power users switch to table-only at one click.
idiot_proof:
A slice returning zero rows names WHICH slice emptied it and offers to remove THAT one — never a bare empty table.
Chart and table row counts are both shown and must match; a mismatch renders a rose banner rather than being silently absorbed.
Saved views are user-named and show their scope (Personal / Public) on the selector. A user must never wonder whether they are looking at everyone's numbers or their own.
Row actions are disabled-with-reason exactly as on LIST/OBJECT — the same action behaves identically wherever it appears.
colours: Chart bars dusty blue #4a7fa5 current, grey baseline/prior. Sage/clay/rose ONLY where a row carries real status. Selected slice at full weight, unselected at ~40% opacity — NEVER a different hue, because hue means status here. Light grey gridlines, no gradients or shadows. Every status paired with glyph and word.
error_display:
A failing chart leaves the TABLE rendering, with rose in the chart panel and a Retry. Losing the visualisation must never cost the user the data.
A filter combination that times out says so and names the expensive filter rather than spinning.
success_display: Saved view: "View 'Joinery overruns' saved (Personal)" in sage. Row actions report through their own screen's success pattern, so wording is identical wherever the user acts.
expected_human_reaction: 10s: "I can see the shape of the problem." 30s: "I have clicked into the worst category and I am looking at the six lines causing it." 60s: "I have raised a variation on one of them without leaving this page." SUCCESS IS ACTING, NOT UNDERSTANDING — understanding is where the dashboard stops.
components_used:
<ScreenFrame> <AnalyticalScreen> <KpiTag> <VisualFilterBar> <FilterBar> <BarChart> <LineChart> <ListScreen> (reused wholesale for the table half) <DrillBreadcrumb> <ViewSelector>.
*** THE TABLE HALF IS <ListScreen>, NOT A NEW TABLE. If it diverges, the same data renders two ways and users will notice. ***
backend_sync:
One aggregate view per KPI tag; one detail view for the table; BOTH DERIVED FROM THE SAME BASE VIEW so chart and table cannot disagree.
Slices are query parameters, so a drilled state has a real URL and is shareable and bookmarkable.
Saved views persist to a saved_views table, org and user scoped, versioned (D-5).
responsive: >=1366 hybrid comfortably. 1024-1365 chart above table stacked. <1024 default switches to TABLE ONLY with a "Show chart" toggle — a chart on a narrow pane is decoration. <768 stacked cards per row; visual filters become a filter sheet.

purpose: Weighted sub-task tree -- GLOBAL's own named exception ("the weighted sub-task BOQ tree"). Real data: 311/655 (47%) of construction.construction_boq_line_items rows are children via parent_line_item_id + breakdown_percentage (verified R42 seq22). A flat ListScreen/ObjectScreen cannot express parent/child rollup with expand/collapse -- CUSTOM is the correct archetype per GLOBAL's own pre-approval, not a registry-model failure.

title: GLOBAL SPEC — DASHBOARD ARCHETYPE
purpose:
*** THERE ARE THREE DISTINCT THINGS AND CONFUSING THEM IS THE COMMONEST ERP UI FAILURE. SAP SEPARATES THEM AND SO DO WE:
 DASHBOARD (SAP Overview Page) = a STARTING POINT FOR ACTION. Cards. SAP: "its main purpose is to serve as a starting point for action or analysis, which is usually COMPLETED IN APPS YOU NAVIGATE TO FROM the overview page." IT IS A LAUNCHPAD, NOT A DESTINATION. The user should LEAVE it within seconds, having learned what needs them.
 ANALYTICAL (SAP Analytical List Page) = EXPLORE AND ACT IN PLACE. Hybrid chart+table, drill down to find a root cause, act on the row you found. See ANALYTICAL.GLOBAL.
 REPORT = A DOCUMENT. Parameterised, fixed layout, exportable, often contractual. See REPORT.GLOBAL.
 TEST: if the user should LEAVE -> dashboard. If they should DIG -> analytical. If they should PRINT OR SEND IT -> report. ***
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Reached from HOME, from a pill, or as the landing route. Breadcrumb "Dashboard · Villa 21". The LEFT pane (Task Master) already answers "what is assigned to me" — THE DASHBOARD MUST NOT DUPLICATE IT (M24 five-band rule). Dashboard answers "what is the STATE OF THE PROJECT", Task Master answers "what is MY MOVE".
document_level: ORG level only. Aggregates across HEADER and ITEM.
input_values:
FILTER BAR, minimal: Period -> RADIO GROUP 4 values (This month / This quarter / YTD / All), default "This month". Project comes from the top rail, NEVER a field. Optional: Category -> multiselect with chips (8+ values).
*** NO OTHER FILTERS. A dashboard with ten filters is an analytical page wearing a costume. ***
displays:
LAYOUT — F-PATTERN, EVIDENCE-BASED: eye-tracking shows top-left gets ~80% of attention, bottom-right under 10%. SPACE RULE 40-30-20-10: 40% to the single most important metric, 30% to 2-3 secondary KPIs, 20% to trend context, 10% to filters/nav.
 TOP-LEFT   THE ONE NUMBER. 2-3x larger than anything else. For PROJEXA that is EARNED VALUE / % COMPLETE BY VALUE.
 TOP-RIGHT  2-3 secondary KPI cards.
 LEFT COL   trends over time.
 RIGHT COL  supporting breakdowns.
 BOTTOM     link-list card (navigation) and any detail table.
KPI CARDS — IDENTICAL LAYOUT ON EVERY CARD (label, value, trend, sparkline in the same positions). EVERY KPI SHOWS THREE THINGS OR IT DOES NOT SHIP:
 1. current value  2. trend direction  3. comparison baseline (target, prior period, or both)
*** "Revenue AED 847,300" WITHOUT a target or trend leaves the user asking "is that good?" — THAT IS A FAILED CARD. Add: target indicator with progress %, a sparkline (7-day or 4-week), and a variance annotation ("15% below plan"). ***
MAX 5-7 KPIs TOTAL (Miller). Tier 1 North Star 3-5 front and centre; Tier 2 supporting 8-12 ONLY if they explain why Tier 1 moved — and those go below the fold.
CHART RULES:
 SPARKLINE beside a KPI for trend — no full chart panel needed.
 BULLET CHART REPLACES GAUGES. Value + target + bands in a compact horizontal bar. Gauges "look impressive but waste space for very little information".
 HORIZONTAL BAR for category comparison, SORTED. Answers "which is worst" instantly.
 LINE for time.
 *** DEMOTE PIE CHARTS. A user cannot tell 20% from 25% in a pie. NEVER a pie with more than 5 segments; prefer a sorted horizontal bar always. ***
 SMALL MULTIPLES for the same chart across categories, instead of overlaying series.
 RULE OF THUMB: if it needs a legend, a tutorial and a deep breath, it is the wrong chart.
DATA-INK (Tufte): light grey gridlines, small axis labels, NO drop shadows, NO gradients, NO rounded chart bars. 30-40% whitespace.
actions:
*** HYPERLINKS ARE THE POINT OF A DASHBOARD — RAJAT 23 AUG. EVERY NUMBER IS A DOOR. ***
 EVERY KPI VALUE IS CLICKABLE and navigates to the ANALYTICAL or REPORT screen that explains it, WITH THE DASHBOARD FILTERS CARRIED THROUGH. Clicking "Earned value 47%" lands on the WPR analytical page already filtered to this project and period.
 EVERY CHART SEGMENT / BAR IS CLICKABLE and drills to the filtered row set (SAP drill-down navigation).
 LINK LIST CARD (SAP pattern) bottom-left: "Quick actions" — Record progress | New BOQ revision | Import BOQ | Run WPR. Each is a function_id, so it opens the real screen, not a popup.
 A KPI WITH NO DESTINATION IS A DEAD END AND MUST NOT SHIP. If a number cannot be explained by another screen, either build that screen or remove the number.
 HEADER: Filter | Export | + New (GLOBAL order). Export = PNG/PDF snapshot of the dashboard as seen, with the filter summary printed on it.
 REFRESH on each card (SAP card action) — reloads that card only, not the page.
next_step: Any KPI click -> ANALYTICAL or REPORT, filters carried. Any quick action -> the FORM or OBJECT screen for that function. Back returns to the dashboard with filters intact.
cognitive_load:
EVERY ELEMENT MAPS TO A DECISION. If a metric does not trigger an action, it does not belong on the screen. This is the test that keeps it at 5-7 KPIs.
CONSISTENT COLOUR MEANING CUTS INTERPRETATION TIME BY UP TO 40% (NN/g). One visual language, applied everywhere.
CONSISTENT TIME RANGES ACROSS ALL CHARTS — mixing daily and monthly on one screen confuses.
PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: summary above the fold, breakdowns below, raw tables one click away and never competing with the headline.
PERFORMANCE IS A DESIGN REQUIREMENT: render KPI cards immediately from cached values, load charts asynchronously. A dashboard taking four seconds is abandoned.
idiot_proof:
IF A FIRST-TIME VIEWER CANNOT IDENTIFY THE PRIMARY METRIC WITHIN FIVE SECONDS, THE HIERARCHY IS BROKEN — that is the acceptance test, run it on Rajat before Sumeet.
No card renders a bare number: value + trend + baseline, always.
Stale data is LABELLED with its timestamp, never shown as if live.
A card with no data says WHY ("No progress recorded this month"), never a blank or a zero that reads as real.
Zero and null are VISUALLY DIFFERENT. A real zero is a fact; a null is missing information. Never render null as 0 — that is how a dashboard lies.
colours:
OUR PASTEL PALETTE MAPS ONTO THE CONVENTIONAL STATUS COLOURS — USE THESE, NOT BRIGHT RED/AMBER/GREEN:
 sage  #5a9178 = on track / improvement / done      (conventional green)
 clay  #c08a4a = at risk / needs attention           (conventional amber)
 rose  #b5748a = off track / late                    (conventional red, ONLY loud colour, sparingly)
 dusty blue #4a7fa5 = neutral / current period / context
 grey  = previous period, baselines, gridlines
*** DIRECTION CONVENTION: up-and-sage = improvement, down-and-rose = decline. FOR LOWER-IS-BETTER METRICS (cost per unit, days late, variance) INVERT THE COLOUR LOGIC so sage still means good. Getting this wrong makes a dashboard actively misleading. ***
*** NEVER COLOUR ALONE (M24 + modern practice): pair with an arrow glyph AND a text status word — "On track" / "At risk" / "Off track". ~8% of men have colour-vision deficiency and construction skews male. A dashboard whose entire logic is red-vs-green excludes part of the audience. ***
Colour means STATUS, never decoration. Blue and grey for neutral. Every colour must communicate something.
error_display:
A card that fails to load shows rose inside ITS OWN CARD with the backend message and a Retry — the rest of the dashboard still renders. ONE FAILING CARD MUST NEVER BLANK THE DASHBOARD.
Footer message area collects card failures with a count.
success_display: Not applicable — a dashboard has no save. Refresh shows the new timestamp on the card, silently.
expected_human_reaction: 5s: "the project is 47% complete by value and one thing is red." 15s: "I clicked the red thing and I am now looking at why." The dashboard has SUCCEEDED WHEN THE USER LEAVES IT — it is a launchpad. A user who stays on the dashboard for two minutes has been given no door to walk through.
components_used: <ScreenFrame> <KpiCard> <Sparkline> <BulletChart> <BarChart> <LineChart> <LinkListCard> <StatusBadge>. All in veridian-ui-kit. Charts via the kit's chosen library, wrapped so the palette and data-ink rules are enforced in ONE place and cannot be overridden per screen.
backend_sync:
Each card = one entry in screen_definitions.columns with its own data_source (an aggregate view) and drill_to (target function_id + param mapping). CARDS LOAD IN PARALLEL, EACH ITS OWN REQUEST, so one slow aggregate cannot block the page.
Aggregates computed SERVER-SIDE in views — never summed in the browser, so the dashboard, the report and any AI answer agree by construction (v5 D-4: the model never computes).
responsive: >=1366 the 40-30-20-10 grid, 12 columns. 1024-1365 secondary KPIs wrap under the primary; charts full width stacked. <1024 SINGLE COLUMN in F-pattern order — primary KPI first. <768 KPI cards full width, sparklines retained, full charts collapse to "View chart" links. THE PRIMARY KPI IS ALWAYS FIRST AT EVERY BREAKPOINT.

title: Project dashboard — the landing screen
purpose: THE FIRST SCREEN SUMEET SEES IN A DEMO AND THE FIRST SCREEN A PM OPENS EVERY MORNING. v5 calls TC-40 "the number Sumeet checks first". Answers ONE question: IS THIS PROJECT WHERE IT SHOULD BE, AND IF NOT, WHERE DO I CLICK.
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Route /(app)/dashboard, which IS PROJEXA's homeRoute — so the LEFT pane renders homeThreadSlot in place of panel (M24). Breadcrumb "Dashboard · Villa 21".
input_values: Period -> RADIO GROUP (This month / This quarter / YTD / All), default "This month". NOTHING ELSE. Project comes from the top rail.
displays:
TOP-LEFT — THE ONE NUMBER, 2-3x larger than anything else on the page:
 *** % COMPLETE BY VALUE, with earned value beneath. TC-30/40/41 anchor: Frame 01 at 30% weight, 50% done on a 5,000 parent -> EARNED 750, PROJECT 15%. THE DASHBOARD MUST SHOW EXACTLY THAT. It is a demo-gate test case, not decoration. ***
 Card carries value + bullet chart against planned + variance annotation ("3% behind plan").
TOP-RIGHT — three secondary KPI cards, identical layout:
 CONTRACT VALUE — PARENT LINES ONLY (v5 D-3), sparkline across revisions. TC-11: 5,000 NOT 10,000.
 BUDGET vs ACTUAL — bullet chart, rose when over.
 PERMITS EXPIRING — count; clay when >0, rose when any expired.
LEFT COLUMN — earned value over time, line, planned as a grey baseline.
RIGHT COLUMN — progress by scope category, SORTED HORIZONTAL BAR. Never a pie.
BOTTOM-LEFT — LINK LIST CARD "Quick actions": Record progress | New revision | Import BOQ | Run WPR.
BOTTOM-RIGHT — five most recent progress entries, each linking to its BOQ line.
actions:
% complete -> ANALYTICAL work-progress, filtered. Contract value -> BOQ OBJECT latest revision. Budget vs actual -> ANALYTICAL cost variance. Permits expiring -> PERMITS.LIST pre-filtered "Expiring 30d". Category bar -> ANALYTICAL filtered to that category. Quick actions -> their FORM screens. Recent entry -> that BOQ line OBJECT.
*** EVERY ONE OF THESE MUST WORK BEFORE THE DEMO. A dashboard with a dead KPI is WORSE than no dashboard: it advertises a capability and breaks in front of the buyer — the unwired-pill failure (v5 P-9 / TC-82) in a new costume. ***
Header: Filter | Export | + New suppressed. Export = PNG/PDF of the dashboard as seen, filter summary printed on it.
next_step: Any KPI or bar click -> ANALYTICAL or LIST with filters carried. Quick action -> FORM. Back -> dashboard, filters intact.
cognitive_load:
ONE dominant number so there is no ambiguity about what matters; everything else is context for it.
Every figure ties to a TC the demo already tests, so dashboard and acceptance tests cannot drift.
No filters beyond period — this is a launchpad, not an analysis tool.
Recent entries give recognition ("yes, that is what I recorded this morning") without running a query.
idiot_proof:
CURRENCY FROM THE ORG SETTING — AED, no rupee sign, no lakh grouping (TC-90). Visible in the first thirty seconds of a demo; getting it wrong is a credibility loss, not a bug.
CONTRACT VALUE SUMS PARENT LINES ONLY. If it ever shows 10,000 for the TC-10 BOQ, B-3 has regressed — THE CARD MUST FAIL LOUDLY RATHER THAN DISPLAY.
Zero state is honest: a project with no progress says "No progress recorded yet — record the first entry" with the action inline, NOT a row of zeros that reads as a stalled project.
colours: Per DASHBOARD.GLOBAL. The one number in near-black at the heaviest weight. Sage/clay/rose only where status is real. Bullet charts dusty blue against grey planned bands.
error_display: Per DASHBOARD.GLOBAL — per-card failure, the rest of the dashboard survives. THE ONE EXCEPTION: if the PRIMARY KPI fails, render a page-level rose banner, because a dashboard without its headline number is not usable and pretending otherwise misleads.
success_display: None — a dashboard has no save. Card refresh updates its timestamp silently.
expected_human_reaction:
5s: "47% by value, AED 2.5m contract, one permit red." 15s: "I have clicked the red permit."
*** SUMEET'S EXPECTED REACTION IN THE DEMO: HE ADDS THE BOQ UP ON PAPER AND THE DASHBOARD AGREES (v5 WO-5 acceptance). That is the moment the product becomes credible — and it is why every number here must come from the same shared helper the report uses. ***
backend_sync:
One aggregate view per card, each its own parallel request so a slow aggregate cannot block the page.
*** EARNED VALUE USES THE SAME SHARED HELPER AS THE WPR REPORT AND construction-reports-service (v5 D-3, ~L119 and ~L660). ONE SUMMATION PATH, NEVER A SECOND. If the dashboard and the report can disagree, B-3 is back. ***
responsive: Per DASHBOARD.GLOBAL. THE PRIMARY KPI IS ALWAYS FIRST AT EVERY BREAKPOINT.

title: GLOBAL SPEC — READ BEFORE ANY OTHER ROW
purpose: Everything every screen shares. Individual rows describe ONLY their differences from this. If a per-screen row contradicts GLOBAL, GLOBAL wins unless the row says "OVERRIDES GLOBAL" and gives a reason. This row is the answer to "how do we reuse components".
fits_right_pane:
M24 FRAME: two panes, LEFT 30% Task Master, RIGHT 70% traditional ERP. Every screen in this table renders in the RIGHT pane ONLY. TOP RAIL ~36px (brand | org | PROJECT tinted click-to-switch | search | alerts | account) is OUTSIDE the pane and is never redrawn by a screen. The COMPOSER is docked full-width across BOTH panes and expands UPWARD over them; a screen must therefore never place anything critical in its own bottom ~120px, and must never assume its full height is visible.
FIVE-BAND RULE (M24), absolute: TOP RAIL=who/where | LEFT HEADER=which slice of my tasks | RIGHT HEADER=what is this screen and what can I do to it | STRIP=what task am I building | INPUT=what am I saying. NOTHING APPEARS TWICE. A screen may NOT grow its own project selector, its own chain, or a second toolbar.
document_level: M31 four levels: ORG (org+project, from top rail, never a field) / HEADER (the document) / ITEM (line items) / SCHEDULE (per-item breakdown or dated entries). Every screen states which levels it renders.
input_values:
CONTROLS BY CARDINALITY (M30, binding): 2 opts=radio pair (or single checkbox if genuinely on/off, NEVER Yes/No radio) | 3-5=radio group all visible | 6-15=select | 16+=searchable combobox | multi 2-7=checkbox group all visible | multi 8+=multiselect with chips | boolean=single checkbox | date=picker NEVER free text | number=numeric + unit label rendered beside it, unit never typed | free text=LAST RESORT only when genuinely unbounded.
NEVER ASKED, ALWAYS DERIVED: project (top rail), organisation (session), entered_by (session), currency (org setting), entry_date (defaults TODAY, editable), rate/amount (derived from the BOQ line — NEVER retyped).
FIELD STATUS per context (M31): REQUIRED | OPTIONAL | SUPPRESSED. Suppressed fields DO NOT RENDER — not greyed, not collapsed, absent. DB check constraint rejects SUPPRESSED+required (SAP rule).
GROUPING: 5-7 fields per section, plain-word headings. Required first and visibly marked; optional collapsed behind "More details", closed by default.
displays:
SHARED CHROME ON EVERY SCREEN:
RIGHT-PANE HEADER: breadcrumb (M24 template) + revision picker where applicable + THE SAME THREE ACTIONS IN THE SAME ORDER ON EVERY SCREEN: Filter | Export | + New.
FOOTER BAR THAT NEVER VANISHES (M29): present even when every action is disabled, because it carries the message area.
MESSAGE AREA in the footer: grouped by section, PERSISTENT, colour = most critical level, shows the error COUNT. NOT a toast.
EMPTY VALUES render as the en-dash (–), never blank.
DOCUMENT FLOW SECTION (M31) on every OBJECT screen: what this came from, what came from it, each a link.
STATUS SHOWN AT BOTH HEADER AND ITEM LEVEL (M31) — a single header status hides what a PM needs.
actions:
ACTION VOCABULARY, SAME WORDS EVERYWHERE — never synonyms:
 Filter | Export | + New            (header, all screens, same order)
 Edit | Save | Cancel | Delete      (object, display/edit)
 Back                               (returns AND RESTORES list filters, sort, scroll, page — M29, mandatory not optional)
 Approve | Confirm | Sign off | Review | Import | Record   (M24 closed verb set, task names start with one)
 Export PDF                         (server-rendered, never browser print; signed URL, 1h)
 EVERY ACTION IS A WORD, NEVER AN ICON ALONE (M24).
 ACTIONS ARE DISABLED BY CONDITION, NEVER HIDDEN, NEVER FAIL-AFTER-CLICK (M29/SAP). A disabled action shows WHY beside it ("2 required fields").
 DESTRUCTIVE ACTIONS ARE NEVER ADJACENT TO COMMON ONES. Delete never sits beside Export.
 DISPLAY FIRST, THEN CHANGE (M31/SAP VA03-before-VA02): object screens OPEN READ-ONLY. Edit is an explicit act.
 DRAFT LIFECYCLE (M29): Edit -> copy active into screen_drafts + 15-min lock (extended on activity) -> autosave debounced ~2s -> Save = validate server-side, write active, DELETE draft, release lock, RE-SELECT AND CONFIRM PERSISTENCE (E-52) -> Cancel = confirm then discard -> LEAVE WITHOUT SAVING = DRAFT KEPT, editing icon beside the title.
 OFFLINE: browser draft via the EXISTING src/lib/offline/work-progress-queue.ts, generalised. On reconnect, if the server draft is NEWER, SURFACE BOTH AND LET THE USER CHOOSE. NEVER SILENTLY OVERWRITE.
next_step: Every screen states its own next step. GLOBAL default: after Save on a create, land on the OBJECT screen for the record just created, in DISPLAY mode, with the success message showing its new id. Never bounce back to an empty form — the user wants to see what they made.
cognitive_load:
COGNITIVE LOAD — GLOBAL MEASURES (M30/M31):
 RECOGNITION OVER RECALL. Never make the user remember a value from another screen. Show it beside the field that needs it.
 THE SCREEN ANSWERS "where am I / what is this / what can I do / what happens next" WITHOUT SCROLLING. If any of the four needs a scroll, the layout is wrong.
 HEADER COPY-DOWN (M31): set unit, date, budget% ONCE on the header, all items inherit. User edits exceptions only. Warn with a COUNT before overwriting manual overrides ("this will change 12 lines, 3 of which you edited").
 CREATE WITH REFERENCE (M31): Rev 2 from Rev 1 copies 153 lines forward. Progress inherits qty/rate/unit/description — the user types ONE number.
 NEVER MAKE A USER CALCULATE. If amount = qty x rate x breakdown%, show it live as they type.
 SHOW THE CONSEQUENCE BEFORE THE ACT, WITH A NUMBER. "This will change 12 lines" is read; "Are you sure?" is clicked through.
 DEFAULT PRE-SELECTED wherever one sensibly exists.
 PROGRESS VISIBLE WITHOUT ASKING: header shows % complete, value, remaining.
 MAX 7 HIGH-IMPORTANCE COLUMNS (M28). An eighth means something else stops being High.
idiot_proof:
IDIOT-PROOF — GLOBAL MEASURES:
 Actions disabled-with-reason, never hidden, never fail-after-click.
 Validate ON BLUR, not per keystroke. Error sits AT THE FIELD, in words saying WHAT TO DO — never "invalid input".
 Primary action disabled while mandatory fields are empty, with the count beside it.
 Initial focus: DISPLAY -> first section. EDIT -> first empty mandatory field; if none, first editable element.
 CREATE mode titled "New <Object>" until a real name/id exists, then replaced.
 Destructive actions require typed or explicit confirm AND state the blast radius ("this BOQ is used by 3 progress entries").
 A click on a task or history entry LOADS THE CHAIN AND STOPS — IT NEVER EXECUTES (M24). Same rule on any screen that can be reached by shortcut.
 SERVER VALIDATES AGAIN, ALWAYS. Client validation is a convenience, never a control.
 TOUCH TARGETS >= 44px; checkbox and radio LABELS clickable, not just the box.
colours:
PALETTE (M24, binding, nothing above ~40% saturation):
 dusty blue #4a7fa5  selection and context
 clay       #c08a4a  your move / needs you
 sage       #5a9178  done / success
 rose       #b5748a  late / error — THE ONLY LOUD COLOUR, USED SPARINGLY
 Background cream (kit token bg-ct-cream). Chrome muted grey.
 TYPE: ONE SIZE ~13px, THREE WEIGHTS. Chain root bold, current step heaviest, earlier steps lighter, chrome muted — you read POSITION without reading WORDS.
 NUMBERS: right-aligned, tabular figures, SAME DECIMAL PLACES DOWN A COLUMN. Misaligned money looks untrustworthy to a QS.
 CURRENCY from the org setting (TC-90). No rupee sign, no lakh grouping for an AED org.
 *** NEVER COLOUR ALONE. Glyph + colour always. Four fixed glyphs in a fixed column: needs-you / running / waiting / done. ~8% of men have colour-vision deficiency and construction skews male. ***
error_display:
ERROR DISPLAY — ONE PATTERN EVERYWHERE:
 COLOUR rose #b5748a. Never red-on-white alarm styling; rose at <40% saturation with a glyph.
 THREE PLACES, EACH A DIFFERENT JOB:
  1. FIELD-LEVEL: text directly under the field, rose, with a glyph. Says what to DO ("Expiry date must be after issue date"), never what is wrong ("invalid").
  2. FOOTER MESSAGE AREA: persistent, grouped by section and table, shows the COUNT, colour reflects the MOST CRITICAL level. Clicking a message SCROLLS TO AND FOCUSES the offending field.
  3. HEADER MESSAGE STRIP: object-level state only ("This BOQ is locked by Suresh until 14:32"). STAYS VISIBLE when the header collapses.
 BACKEND MESSAGES ARE RELAYED VERBATIM (veridian-client already does this). Never replace a real backend message with a generic one — that is R-90/F-15.
 A FAILED SAVE NEVER LOSES THE FORM. Values stay, draft stays, lock stays.
 NEVER A BARE TOAST FOR AN ERROR. Toasts vanish; errors must persist until resolved.
success_display:
SUCCESS DISPLAY:
 COLOUR sage #5a9178 with a check glyph.
 INLINE AND SPECIFIC, NEVER A BARE "Saved": state WHAT and give the ID — "Permit PMT-0043 created" / "Progress recorded: 61.60 m2 on 1.01, now 279.10 of 600".
 Success message lives in the footer message area, sage, and CLEARS on the next user action rather than on a timer — the user decides when they have read it.
 AFTER A CREATE: land on the new record in DISPLAY mode with its id visible. The record itself is the confirmation.
 AUTOSAVE IS SILENT — no message. A visible "saved" every 2 seconds is noise. The editing icon beside the title is the only signal a draft exists.
expected_human_reaction:
EXPECTED HUMAN REACTION — the design target for every screen:
 FIRST 3 SECONDS: "I know what this screen is and which project it belongs to" — without reading body text. Breadcrumb + title + tinted project in the top rail do this.
 FIRST 10 SECONDS: "I can see what I have to do" — the primary action is visually dominant and either enabled, or disabled with a stated reason.
 ON ERROR: "I know exactly which field and what to type" — not "something went wrong somewhere".
 ON SAVE: "I can see the thing I just made, with its number" — not a return to a blank form.
 ON INTERRUPTION: "my work is still here" — draft survived a phone call, a tunnel, a browser crash.
 ON RETURN FROM A DETAIL: "my filtered list is exactly as I left it".
 THE FEELING TO AVOID: hesitation. If a user pauses to work out what a control does, that control has failed.
components_used:
COMPONENT REUSE — THIS IS THE ANSWER TO "how to reuse components".
 ALL SHARED COMPONENTS LIVE IN veridian-ui-kit (branch MASTER, not main). PROJEXA and compliance-tracker both consume them. NOTHING module-specific is written in projexa.
 <ScreenFrame>    breadcrumb, three header actions, footer bar, message area, mode handling, focus rules
 <ListScreen>     table, filters, importance-driven columns, drill_to, back-state restore
 <ObjectScreen>   dynamic header + facets + status strip, anchor/tab sections, document-flow section, draft lifecycle, dual status
 <FormSection>    5-7 fields, plain-word heading, required-first, optional collapsed
 <FieldRenderer>  the M30 control table — the ONLY place a control is chosen
 <MessageArea>    the three error places
 <DocumentFlow>   ancestors and children as links
 <StatusBadge>    glyph + colour, never colour alone
 <MoneyCell>      right-aligned tabular, org currency, fixed decimals
 *** IF A MODULE NEEDS A BESPOKE COMPONENT, THE ARCHETYPE IS WRONG. REPORT IT RATHER THAN WRITING THE COMPONENT. That is the test that keeps this from becoming 330 screens. Expected exceptions: 5-10 CUSTOM screens out of ~80 (the weighted sub-task BOQ tree, the variation diff). ***
backend_sync:
BACKEND/FRONTEND SYNC — HOW THEY CANNOT DRIFT:
 ONE REGISTRY, TWO CONSUMERS (M28): compliance.screen_definitions.columns[].options_source IS THE SAME QUERY Level 1 is given as its candidate set. A dropdown and the AI cannot disagree because they read one definition.
 READ PATH: browser route -> projexa API route (requireAuth, org from session) -> callVeridian(resource) Bearer+org-scoped -> VERIDIAN service -> compliance.<table> under RLS (org_id = current_org_id()).
 WRITE PATH: form -> client validate (convenience) -> autosave draft -> Save -> POST/PATCH -> projexa route -> callVeridian -> service VALIDATES AGAIN -> write -> delete draft -> release lock -> RE-SELECT AND CONFIRM (E-52).
 FILES IN: <input type=file> -> FormData -> projexa route -> callVeridianUpload (MULTIPART, never base64-through-JSON) -> VERIDIAN -> Supabase Storage bucket -> row carrying storage_path.
 FILES OUT: createSignedUrl(storage_path, 3600). NEVER getPublicUrl.
 TYPE SAFETY: the screen renders from screen_definitions; if a column named there does not exist in data_source, the screen must FAIL LOUDLY AT LOAD with the column name — not render a blank. Metadata-driven means the data model must be honest (M28).
responsive:
RESPONSIVE — the right pane is ~70% of the viewport, so it is NARROWER than a full page:
 >=1366px  right pane ~950px. All columns per importance. Sections side by side where they fit.
 1024-1365 right pane ~700px. Low-importance columns DROP (M28 progressive disclosure). Sections stack.
 <1024     the two panes STACK: Task Master collapses to a summary bar, the ERP screen takes full width. This is the site-engineer-on-a-phone case.
 <768      table archetypes switch from columns to STACKED CARDS, one record per card, showing only High-importance fields. Filters move behind a Filter sheet.
 THE COMPOSER IS DOCKED AND EXPANDS UPWARD ON EVERY BREAKPOINT — no screen may place a primary action in its own bottom 120px.
 TOUCH TARGETS >=44px at every breakpoint, not just mobile.
 NO HORIZONTAL SCROLLING ON A TABLE, EVER. Drop columns by importance instead.

title: Permits register
purpose: The register a site/QS person opens to answer one question: what is expiring and do I need to act. NOT a filing cabinet — an alert surface that happens to also list everything.
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Breadcrumb "Permits · Villa 21". No left-rail entry (M24 removes the rail); reached by pill Permits, by HOME module card, or by a task row click.
document_level: ORG (project from top rail) + HEADER rows only. No items.
input_values:
FILTERS (M30 cardinality): Status — 4 values (Valid / Expiring 30d / Expired / All) -> RADIO GROUP, all visible, default "All". Authority — 6-15 values -> SELECT. Issue date range -> two DATE PICKERS. Search by permit name/number -> text (genuinely unbounded, allowed).
NO PROJECT FIELD — it comes from the top rail (GLOBAL).
displays:
COLUMNS, importance-ranked (max 7 High per M28):
 High:   glyph+status | Permit no. | Name | Authority | Issue date | Expiry date | Days left
 Medium: Uploaded by | File (paperclip + size)
 Low:    Created at | Last modified
"Days left" is DERIVED and is the whole point of the screen — rose when negative, clay when <=30, sage otherwise, ALWAYS with its glyph.
Row count and active filter summary shown above the table ("12 permits · Expiring 30d").
actions:
HEADER: Filter | Export | + New (GLOBAL order).
ROW CLICK -> PERMITS.OBJECT display mode. Never a popup.
Export -> CSV of the CURRENT FILTERED SET, not everything. Filename includes project and date.
NO inline edit, NO row-level delete on the list. Destructive and mutating actions live on the object screen where the user can see the whole record first (M31 display-before-change).
cognitive_load:
The default filter is "All" but the table is SORTED BY DAYS LEFT ASCENDING — expiring things surface without the user choosing a filter. Recognition over recall.
Status is a 4-value radio group, all visible: the user never clicks to discover what states exist (Hick).
"Days left" is computed and displayed so the user never subtracts dates in their head.
Back from the object restores filters, sort, scroll and page (GLOBAL, mandatory).
idiot_proof:
Empty state PROMPTS, never looks broken: "No permits recorded for Villa 21 yet — add the first one" with the + New action inline.
Filtered-to-empty is DIFFERENT and says so: "No permits match Expired — clear filters", with a Clear filters action. Confusing these two is a classic ERP dead end.
Export disabled with reason when the filtered set is empty.
colours: Sage for valid, clay for expiring within 30 days, rose for expired — each with its own glyph, never colour alone. Dates and Days-left right-aligned tabular. Cream background, muted chrome.
error_display:
Load failure: footer message area, rose, backend message verbatim, with a Retry action. The table shell still renders with column headers so the screen does not look broken.
A permit row whose file is missing from storage shows the paperclip in rose with tooltip "File not found" — the row still renders. One bad file must never blank the register.
success_display: Not applicable on load. After returning from a create, the footer carries the sage success from PERMITS.OBJECT ("Permit PMT-0043 created") and the new row is highlighted for one interaction.
expected_human_reaction: 3s: "these are Villa 21 permits and two are red." 10s: "the red ones are at the top, I know what to chase." The user should be able to leave after 3 seconds having got the answer — the register is the by-product, the alert is the product.
components_used: <ScreenFrame> <ListScreen> <StatusBadge> <MoneyCell> not needed. Zero bespoke components — if any are needed the archetype is wrong.

*** ALREADY BUILT AND VERIFIED 23 Aug: projexa/src/app/api/permits/route.ts GET+POST exist on origin/main. compliance.documents has 216 rows with category values including permit. DO NOT BUILD A PERMITS TABLE. ***
Days-left is computed SERVER-SIDE in the data_source view so the list, the export and any AI candidate set all agree.
responsive: >=1366 all columns. 1024-1365 drop Low (created/modified). <1024 full width, drop Medium. <768 STACKED CARDS: status glyph + name + expiry + days left only; filters behind a Filter sheet. Never horizontal scroll.

title: Permit — display / edit / create
purpose: One permit, whole, on its own URL. The screen a user lands on from the register, from a task, or from a shared link. Same layout in all three modes (M31/SAP VA01-02-03).
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Breadcrumb "Permits · Villa 21 · PMT-0043". Own route /(app)/permits/[id]. Create uses /permits/new.
document_level: ORG (top rail) + HEADER only. Permits have no line items — this is the simplest OBJECT and therefore the right one to build first.
input_values:
SECTION 1 "Permit details" (required, 5 fields):
 Permit name    TEXT (unbounded, allowed)
 Permit number  TEXT — auto-suggested next in series, editable
 Authority      SELECT (6-15 known authorities) — the list is options_source, shared with Level 1
 Issue date     DATE PICKER, defaults TODAY
 Expiry date    DATE PICKER, no default (a wrong default here is dangerous)
SECTION 2 "Document" (required):
 File           multipart upload, PDF/JPG/PNG, max size stated BEFORE selection
SECTION 3 "More details" (optional, COLLAPSED by default):
 Notes          TEXTAREA
 Tags           CHECKBOX GROUP (2-7 values, all visible)
NEVER ASKED: project, org, uploaded_by, created_at (all derived — GLOBAL).
displays:
DYNAMIC HEADER: title = permit name (or "New Permit" until named, M29), subtitle = permit number, STATUS BADGE glyph+colour, header facets = Authority · Issue · Expiry · Days left.
MESSAGE STRIP under the title for object-level state, stays visible when the header collapses: "Locked by Suresh until 14:32" or "Expires in 12 days".
FILE PREVIEW inline (PDF first page / image thumbnail) via createSignedUrl(path, 3600) — NEVER getPublicUrl.
DOCUMENT FLOW section: nothing upstream for a permit; downstream shows any task referencing it. Present even when empty, reading "Not linked to any other document" — absence is information.
actions:
DISPLAY MODE footer: Edit | Export PDF | Delete (Delete separated by a gap from the others — GLOBAL destructive rule).
EDIT MODE footer: Save | Cancel. Save disabled while required fields are empty, WITH THE COUNT beside it ("2 required fields").
CREATE MODE footer: Save | Cancel. Title reads "New Permit" until the name is typed.
BACK returns to PERMITS.LIST with filters, sort, scroll and page restored.
EXPORT PDF: server-rendered permit sheet, signed URL 1h. Never browser print.
DELETE: confirm stating blast radius ("PMT-0043 is referenced by 2 tasks"). If referenced, delete is DISABLED with that reason rather than allowed and then failing.
DRAFT LIFECYCLE exactly per GLOBAL — Edit takes a 15-min lock, autosave ~2s, leaving keeps the draft and shows the editing icon.
next_step: Save on create -> stay on this screen, switch to DISPLAY mode, success shows the new number. Save on edit -> DISPLAY mode, same record. Cancel -> DISPLAY mode if editing an existing record, or back to LIST if creating.
cognitive_load:
Opens READ-ONLY. Edit is an explicit act (M31 display-before-change) — the user cannot accidentally alter a permit they only wanted to look at.
Expiry date sits DIRECTLY BESIDE issue date with the interval shown live as they pick ("11 months") — no mental date arithmetic.
Days left is derived and always visible in the header facets.
Only 5 required fields, in one section, required-first. Optional fields collapsed so the initial screen shows exactly what must be done.
File size limit stated BEFORE the user selects a file, not as an error after a 30-second upload on site 4G.
idiot_proof:
Save disabled with a count until required fields are filled.
Expiry-before-issue is caught ON BLUR at the field, in words: "Expiry date must be after the issue date."
Upload rejects wrong type at selection with the allowed list, not after upload.
Leaving mid-edit keeps the draft — the user cannot lose work by navigating away or being interrupted.
Delete disabled-with-reason when referenced. Never allowed-then-failed.
On a locked record the whole screen is read-only with the lock reason in the message strip, and Edit is disabled with that reason.
colours: Status badge sage valid / clay expiring / rose expired, glyph always. Header facets muted grey labels with normal-weight values. Required-field marker clay, not rose — rose is reserved for actual errors and must not be diluted by decoration.
error_display:
Field errors under the field, rose + glyph, imperative wording.
Footer message area groups by section, shows the count, and clicking a message scrolls to and focuses that field.
Upload failure keeps the form and the draft intact and states the backend message verbatim.
Lock conflict shows in the header message strip with the holder and the expiry time — never a bare "could not edit".
success_display:
"Permit PMT-0043 created" in the footer, sage with a check glyph, clearing on the next action rather than on a timer. The record itself is the confirmation — the user is looking at what they made.
Autosave is SILENT; the editing icon beside the title is the only draft signal.
expected_human_reaction:
3s: "this is permit PMT-0043 for Villa 21 and it expires in 12 days." 10s: "I can edit it, export it, and I can see the actual document." On save: "there it is, with its number." On interruption: "my half-typed permit is still here."
The reaction to avoid: uncertainty about whether the file uploaded. The inline preview is what removes that doubt.
components_used: <ScreenFrame> <ObjectScreen> <FormSection> <FieldRenderer> <MessageArea> <DocumentFlow> <StatusBadge>. Zero bespoke. Permits is the simplest OBJECT — if it needs a bespoke component the archetype is wrong and everything downstream is at risk.

GET  /api/permits/[id]  -> callVeridian /permits/[id] -> compliance.documents (category=permit) under RLS
POST /api/permits       -> callVeridianUpload MULTIPART (already exists on origin/main)
PATCH /api/permits/[id] -> callVeridian
File in: FormData -> callVeridianUpload -> Supabase Storage bucket -> row carries storage_path.
File out: createSignedUrl(storage_path, 3600).
Draft: compliance.screen_drafts, UNIQUE (function_id, object_id) enforcing one draft per record IN THE DATABASE.
Save re-SELECTs and confirms persistence before reporting success (E-52).
responsive: >=1366 sections side by side, file preview right. 1024-1365 sections stack, preview below. <1024 full width. <768 header facets wrap to two lines, preview collapses to a "View document" action, footer actions become full-width stacked buttons. Composer still docked — nothing critical in the bottom 120px.

title: GLOBAL SPEC — REPORT ARCHETYPE
purpose:
A REPORT IS A DOCUMENT, NOT A SCREEN. It is parameterised, has a FIXED layout, and its output is meant to be EXPORTED, PRINTED, SIGNED OR SENT. Sumeet's WPR goes to a client as part of a payment application — it is contractual. A dashboard is for deciding; A REPORT IS FOR PROVING.
*** THE TEST THAT SEPARATES IT FROM A DASHBOARD: WOULD SOMEONE PRINT THIS AND PUT IT IN A FILE, OR ATTACH IT TO AN INVOICE? Then it is a report and its layout is fixed, not explorable. ***
fits_right_pane: Right pane, full. Breadcrumb "Reports · WPR · Villa 21 · Jul 2026". Reached from the Reports pill, from a dashboard KPI click (parameters pre-filled), or from a task.
document_level: Aggregates HEADER + ITEM + SCHEDULE. A report is usually the only place all three levels appear together.
input_values:
PARAMETER BAR — a report is DEFINED by its parameters and they are always visible:
 Period       -> two DATE PICKERS or a month SELECT. Defaults to the last closed period, NOT today (a half-finished month is not a report).
 BOQ revision -> SELECT, defaults to LATEST APPROVED (TC-43: only the latest revision counts).
 Grouping     -> RADIO GROUP 3-5 values (By scope / By category / By trade), default "By scope".
 Include      -> CHECKBOX GROUP, all visible (Sub-tasks / Photos / Variations / Retention).
*** PARAMETERS ARE PART OF THE OUTPUT. Every export prints its parameters in the header. A report without its parameters visible cannot be audited, and Sumeet's QS WILL ask which revision a number came from. ***
displays:
FIXED TABULAR LAYOUT — this is the AIA G703 continuation-sheet shape Sumeet already uses (M25 research), and it must not be "improved":
 Item | Description | Unit | Qty | Rate | SCHEDULED VALUE | PREVIOUS | THIS PERIOD | TOTAL TO DATE | % | BALANCE
 with the arithmetic identity PREVIOUS + THIS PERIOD = TOTAL TO DATE and % = TOTAL / SCHEDULED, both VISIBLY TRUE on the page.
 GROUP SUBTOTALS and a GRAND TOTAL that ties. *** IF THE SUBTOTALS DO NOT SUM TO THE GRAND TOTAL THE REPORT IS WRONG AND MUST SAY SO LOUDLY, not render anyway. ***
 PARENT LINES ONLY in the value column (v5 D-3); child weights drive progress. A report that double-counts sub-tasks is the B-3 defect on paper.
 Sub-task rows INDENTED under their parent, collapsible, off by default (the "Include sub-tasks" checkbox).
 HEADER BLOCK on every page: project, client, revision, period, parameters, generated-at, generated-by.
 SPARKLINE per group is permitted; NO other chart. A report is read as numbers, not scanned as shapes.
 ROW COUNT AND TOTALS ALWAYS VISIBLE, never requiring a scroll to the bottom.
actions:
HEADER: Filter (opens the parameter bar) | Export | + New not applicable — SUPPRESSED, not greyed (a report is not created from a report).
 EXPORT PDF — server-rendered, page-numbered, parameters in the header, signed URL 1h. NEVER browser print: browser print breaks column alignment and that is a contractual document.
 EXPORT XLSX — raw rows so a QS can check the arithmetic himself. THIS IS A TRUST FEATURE, NOT A CONVENIENCE.
 SHARE LINK — the existing share-link service (PR #1331), token-scoped, expiring.
 *** EVERY ITEM CODE IN THE TABLE IS A HYPERLINK to that BOQ line's OBJECT screen. Every group subtotal links to the ANALYTICAL page filtered to that group. A QS asking "where does 20,833.20 come from" must be ONE CLICK from the answer, not an email to Sumeet. ***
 REGENERATE with changed parameters — never edits in place; a report is a snapshot of its parameters.
next_step: Item code click -> BOQ line OBJECT. Subtotal click -> ANALYTICAL filtered. Export -> file. Share -> link. Back -> wherever the user came from, with state.
cognitive_load:
PARAMETERS DEFAULT TO THE COMMON CASE (last closed period, latest approved revision) so the user runs the report by pressing nothing.
THE ARITHMETIC IS SHOWN, NOT ASSERTED: Previous + This period = Total is visible across the row, so the user verifies by reading rather than trusting.
GROUPING IS A 3-5 RADIO GROUP, all visible — the user sees every way this report can be cut without clicking.
The layout NEVER CHANGES between runs. A report the user has read once is read faster every time after. THIS IS WHY EXPLORATION BELONGS IN ANALYTICAL, NOT HERE.
idiot_proof:
A report over an unapproved or superseded revision shows a clay banner naming the revision — never silently reports on a draft.
Empty period says "No progress recorded between 1 and 31 Jul" with the parameters echoed — never a blank table.
If any subtotal fails to tie, a ROSE banner at the top states the discrepancy and the export is DISABLED with that reason. A report that does not add up must never leave the building.
Export disabled with reason while the table is empty.
colours: Rose only for a failed total or a data error. Clay for a revision warning. Otherwise MONOCHROME AND DENSE — a report is not a dashboard and colour here is noise. Numbers right-aligned, tabular figures, identical decimals down every column. Group subtotal rows in a slightly heavier weight, grand total heaviest. Print stylesheet: no background fills, black text, visible column rules.
error_display:
Generation failure: rose in the footer message area with the backend message verbatim and a Retry. Parameters are PRESERVED — never make a user re-enter a period after a failure.
A row whose source line was deleted renders with a rose marker and a note rather than silently vanishing. A missing row changes a total, and a total that changed without explanation destroys trust.
success_display: "Report generated · 153 lines · AED 2,500,000 · 47.2%" in the footer, sage, clearing on the next action. After Export: "WPR-Jul-2026.pdf ready" with the download link inline.
expected_human_reaction: 10s: "these are my numbers, in the shape I know, for the period I expected." On a query: "I clicked the line and I can see exactly where it came from." The reaction to design for is a QS being ABLE TO CHECK IT — trust comes from verifiability, not from polish. The reaction to avoid: "which revision is this?"
components_used: <ScreenFrame> <ReportTable> <ParameterBar> <MoneyCell> <Sparkline>. <ReportTable> is shared across every report; individual reports are registry rows, NOT components.
backend_sync:
GET /api/reports/[reportId]?params -> callVeridian -> a REPORT DEFINITION EXECUTED SERVER-SIDE (v5 D-5/F-5: report definitions are stored as DATA and runnable by id, already exists). SQL is SELECT-only and org-scoped.
Totals computed SERVER-SIDE. The browser never sums — dashboard, report and AI must agree by construction.
PDF rendered server-side; stored to the bucket; returned as a signed URL (1h).
responsive: >=1366 all columns. 1024-1365 drop Rate and Unit (recoverable from the line item). <1024 the report becomes SCROLLABLE HORIZONTALLY AS ONE UNIT — *** THIS IS THE ONE ARCHETYPE WHERE HORIZONTAL SCROLL IS PERMITTED, BECAUSE THE COLUMN SET IS CONTRACTUAL AND DROPPING A COLUMN WOULD CHANGE THE DOCUMENT. It OVERRIDES the GLOBAL no-horizontal-scroll rule, and only here. *** <768 offer "Export PDF" prominently — reading a G703 on a phone is not a real use case; sending one is.
